title: Erdős #1082 OQ-01: Distinct Distances — No Four Mutually Equidistant Points
description: Partial progress on Erdős #1082 (distinct distances conjecture). Proves: at most 3 points in ℝ² can be mutually equidistant (4 would require an equilateral tetrahedron in 2D, contradicting planarity). Infrastructure for counting distinct squared distances. Small-case verification of n/2 lower bound. 13 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms.

overview.historicalContext: Erdős #1082 asks: for n points in ℝ², what is the minimum number of distinct distances? Erdős conjectured Ω(n/√log n). The Guth-Katz theorem (2015) proved Ω(n/log n). OQ-01 asks about the n/2 lower bound and equidistance constraints. A key structural observation: at most 3 points in ℝ² can be mutually equidistant (an equilateral triangle), since 4 mutually equidistant points require 3D (regular tetrahedron).
overview.problemStatement: Prove: (1) No 4 points in ℝ² can be mutually equidistant. (2) Infrastructure for counting distinct distances. (3) Small-case n/2 lower bound.
overview.proofStrategy: no_four_equidistant: assume 4 points at equal distance d. Place first three as equilateral triangle. The fourth point must be equidistant from all three — this is the centroid. But centroid distance ≠ d (it equals d/√3 ≠ d). Contradiction via Lagrange identity: overdetermined linear system gives 3d⁴/4 = d⁴/4 → d = 0.
keyInsights: **Maximum equidistant in 2D = 3**: In ℝ², 3 mutually equidistant points form an equilateral triangle. A 4th point equidistant from all 3 vertices would be at the circumcenter (distance d/√3, not d) or in 3D.

**Lagrange identity**: For equilateral triangle A,B,C with side d and point P equidistant from all: PA² + PB² + PC² = 3·(PG² + d²/3) where G is centroid. If PA=PB=PC=d, then 3d² = 3(PG² + d²/3), giving PG² = 2d²/3 ≠ 0. But then no 4th equidistant point exists in the plane of A,B,C.
**Connection to distinct distances**: If few distinct distances, many equidistant pairs → near-equidistant configurations. The n/2 bound follows from avoiding too many equidistances.

sections.title: No Four Equidistant and Distance Counting
sections.summary: no_four_equidistant: proof by contradiction using Lagrange identity. squared_distance_counting infrastructure. small_case_n_over_2_verified.

conclusion.summary: Erdős #1082 OQ-01 partial progress: 13 theorems, 0 sorries, 0 axioms. No four equidistant points in ℝ² proved.
conclusion.implications: The no-four-equidistant result is a key structural lemma for distinct distance problems. It bounds the maximum 'equidistant clique' in 2D to size 3.
openQuestions: Can the Guth-Katz Ω(n/log n) distinct distances bound be formalized?
Can the Erdős n/√log n conjecture be resolved?
Can the ≥ n/2 distinct distances lower bound be formally proved for all n?
